lines.text: Raw placeholders were jarring in a catalog context. When a landing page links straight to source templates, browsers see unfilled scaffolding instead of the finished document. The fix is a separation rule: authoring artifacts and browsing artifacts are different things.
Before, landing rows exposed raw source files. After, every row opens a filled demo built for browsing. Authoring stays in templates; browsing gets representative, finished mock content.

The catalog contract has four parts. Document mocks give every core type a filled preview. Diagram mocks keep chart primitives separate. And the regression guard, landing-links dot test, is the durable contract: it rejects raw source folders and validates every linked file.
One principle to take away: placeholders are healthy in source templates, and wrong in landing demos. Keep the seam explicit and the catalog stays honest.
The numbers: five document rows, thirty nine diagram rows, one test boundary. Future template additions link through the same contract.
